standard_prerequisites.name: The square and cube lemma for a ring extension: an element outside the subring with two consecutive powers inside can be replaced by one whose square and cube lie inside
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cited at proof lines 11730-11733, this being the lane's card L34015 (lemma-nth-and-nplusone-implies-square-and-cube)
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the element adjoined at each successor stage of the transfinite construction.

standard_prerequisites.name: Behaviour of the properties at hand under filtered colimits of rings: a colimit inherits the property, and both universal closedness and inducing isomorphisms on residue fields are stable under composition
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the implication from the tower condition to the single-generator case.

standard_prerequisites.name: An integral ring extension gives a universally closed and surjective morphism of spectra, cited from the same chapter and the algebra chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides universal closedness and surjectivity in the single-generator case.

standard_prerequisites.name: The characterizations of a universal homeomorphism and of universal injectivity, cited from the same chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts bijectivity on points plus isomorphisms on residue fields plus universal closedness into the assertion of (1).

core_obligations: Transfinite construction from (1): build A-subalgebras by recursion, starting from A, taking filtered colimits at limit ordinals, and at a successor ordinal adjoining, when the algebra is not yet all of B, an element outside it whose square and cube lie inside, which exists by the cited square and cube lemma; the union of the chain is B (indeed the process stops by a cardinality argument) (proof lines 11726-11738).

Transfinite induction for the tower condition: prove by induction that the tower condition holds for each member of the chain; the case of a limit ordinal reduces a finite set to one member of the chain, and at a successor ordinal one writes each element of the finite set as a polynomial in the adjoined element with coefficients in the previous member, collects the coefficients together with the square and cube of the adjoined element, and extends the tower given by the induction hypothesis by one more element (proof lines 11739-11751).

Reduction for the converse: write the algebra as the filtered colimit of its finite subalgebras; by the colimit stability statement it suffices to treat each finite subalgebra, and by stability under composition it suffices to treat an algebra generated by a single element whose square and cube lie in the base (proof lines 11753-11759).

Single generator case: such an extension is integral, hence the morphism of spectra is universally closed and surjective; the relation between the square and the cube of the generator holds in the base, and for any base field every image of the generator is either zero or determined by the quotient of its cube by its square, so the base changed algebra is a quotient of a ring with a single prime and residue field that field; hence the morphism is bijective and induces isomorphisms on residue fields, which together with universal closedness gives the first condition (proof lines 11760-11782).
proof_roadmap: From the geometric condition, build a transfinite chain of subalgebras whose union is the whole algebra, adjoining at each step an element with square and cube one stage down, and verify the tower condition by transfinite induction (proof lines 11726-11751).

For the converse, reduce by filtered colimits and composition to a single generator with square and cube in the base, where integrality gives universal closedness and surjectivity and the explicit description of the base change to any field gives bijectivity and isomorphisms on residue fields (proof lines 11753-11782).
difficulty_reason: The proposition characterizes the ring extensions whose spectrum map is a universal homeomorphism inducing isomorphisms on residue fields by a tower condition: every finite set of elements lies in a subalgebra built by adjoining elements whose square and cube lie one stage down (statement lines 11712-11724). The counted proof has two genuinely different halves: the forward direction is a transfinite recursion that builds a chain of subalgebras by repeatedly adjoining an element supplied by the square-and-cube lemma, together with a transfinite induction verifying the tower condition at limit and successor ordinals; the converse reduces by filtered colimits and stability under composition to the case of a single generator with square and cube in the base, where integrality gives universal closedness and surjectivity while an explicit analysis of the base change to any field shows bijectivity on points and isomorphisms on residue fields (proof lines 11726-11782). It is H2: both directions are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being the square-and-cube lemma, colimit stability and the standard integrality and homeomorphism criteria.
